**Title:** Drive Today, Collect Tomorrow: How the "Hot List" Redefines Future Classics

For decades, the world of car collecting has felt like an exclusive club reserved for the ultra-wealthy. With vintage Ferraris, air-cooled Porsches, and mint-condition American muscle cars fetching astronomical prices at auction, average automotive enthusiasts are often priced out of the hobby before they even begin. Recognizing this growing barrier to entry, specialty valuation expert McKeel Hagerty set out to democratize car collecting by shifting the market’s focus from the past to the present. 

Hagerty’s solution was the creation of the annual "Hot List"—a carefully curated forecast designed to identify modern, mass-production vehicles destined to become the highly sought-after classics of tomorrow. Rather than relying on hindsight, Hagerty developed a predictive formula based on three core pillars: pop culture relevance, limited production numbers, and unique, striking design style. By analyzing these factors early in a vehicle's life cycle, the Hot List highlights cars that possess that elusive "it" factor—the emotional spark that turns an everyday vehicle into an automotive icon.

The brilliance of the Hot List lies in the diversity and character of its selections. Take, for example, the **Cadillac XLR-V Roadster**. With its bold, stealth-fighter angular styling, retractable hardtop, and supercharged Northstar V8 engine, the XLR-V represented a daring era of American luxury performance. Its low production numbers and distinctive place in mid-2000s pop culture make it a prime candidate for future appreciation.

On the opposite end of the spectrum sits the **Lotus Exige S**. Stripped of unnecessary weight and built purely for driver engagement, the Exige S represents an increasingly rare breed of uncompromising, analog track weapons. As the automotive industry shifts toward heavy electronics and electrification, lightweight purists' cars like the Exige S are virtually guaranteed a permanent place in the collector pantheon.

Then there is the **Audi S5**, a vehicle that proves a future classic can also be a masterclass in subtlety. Styled by legendary designer Walter de Silva, the original S5 Coupe combined timeless, flowing proportions with a high-revving V8 engine and all-weather Quattro utility. It is a car that captures the perfect balance of understated elegance and usable performance.

What truly makes Hagerty’s philosophy compelling is its practical value proposition. The traditional approach to car collecting requires buying a delicate vintage vehicle, spending thousands on upkeep, and leaving it tucked away in a climate-controlled garage. The Hot List turns this model on its head. By identifying future classics while they are still modern, consumers are given permission to enjoy these exciting vehicles as daily drivers today. 

Over a 15-to-20-year horizon, as the typical depreciation curve bottoms out and modern examples are inevitably lost to accidents or neglect, pristine models transition from "used cars" to cherished collectibles. For today's car lover, this means the thrill of driving a standout machine every morning comes with a built-in financial bonus: the knowledge that their daily commute is also a smart, long-term investment.

**From Dial-Up to Die-Cast: How AOL Transformed the World of Auto Collecting**

There was a time in the late 1990s when the thrilling screech of a 56k modem was the gateway to the world. For hobbyists of that era, clicking on the iconic yellow running man icon of **AOL** (America Online) wasn't just about checking email or entering a chat room; it was the beginning of a revolution in how people pursued their passions—especially when it came to **autos** and **collecting**.

Before the rise of the modern internet, collecting automobiles or automotive memorabilia was a localized, labor-intensive pursuit. Whether you were hunting for a pristine 1967 Mustang, searching for a rare carburetor for a restoration project, or scouring markets for vintage die-cast Hot Wheels, your options were limited. Collectors relied on local newspaper classifieds, physical swap meets, specialized print magazines, and word-of-mouth. Finding that one missing piece to complete a collection could take years of patient searching.

Then came AOL, bringing millions of households online for the first time. 

With the simple entry of a phrase into the search bar—like *Keyword: Autos*—the world of collecting suddenly shrunk. AOL’s message boards and interest groups became the digital equivalent of a 24/7 global car show. Enthusiasts who had spent decades feeling isolated in their niche auto-collecting subgenres suddenly found thriving online communities. 

On AOL's automotive forums, a classic car collector in Ohio could advice-share with a mechanic in Munich. A fan collecting vintage oil cans or porcelain gas station signs could trade directly with someone thousands of miles away. It democratized the hobby, establishing price benchmarks, exposing counterfeits, and making rare auto parts accessible with a few clicks and a "You've Got Mail!" notification.

Fascinatingly, history has now come full circle. Today, the very medium that changed auto collecting has itself become a target for collectors. Nostalgic tech enthusiasts now search vintage markets for unopened AOL free-trial CD-ROMs—those ubiquitous tins and sleeves that used to flood mailboxes in the '90s—treating them with the same historical appreciation that auto enthusiasts reserve for vintage license plates or classic car brochures.

While technology has evolved far beyond the walled garden of AOL, the foundation it laid remains intact. Modern digital auctions and social media groups for auto collecting owe their existence to those early dial-up days. AOL proved that collecting autos was never just about the metal, paint, or horsepower—it was about the community of people connected by a shared passion.

counterfactuals.prompt: What modern cars are predicted to become future collectibles according to car valuation experts like Hagerty?
counterfactuals.output:
Automotive valuation experts like **Hagerty** (famous for their annual *Bull Market List*), **Bring a Trailer** trends, and **Barrett-Jackson** analysts regularly track which modern cars (roughly 2000s–2020s) are transitioning from simple used cars into sought-after collectibles. 

The primary drivers for modern collectibility right now are **the death of the manual transmission**, **the shift to electric vehicles (EVs)**, and **Millennial/Gen-Z nostalgia** for the cars of their youth.

Here are the top modern cars predicted by experts to become future collectibles, categorized by type:

---

### 1. The "Last of the Analog" Sports Cars
As cars become more computer-driven and turbocharged, raw, naturally aspirated, manual-transmission sports cars are skyrocketing in value.

*   **Porsche Cayman GT4 / Boxster Spyder (981 & 718 Generations):** Hagerty consistently highlights these. They feature naturally aspirated flat-six engines paired with manual gearboxes, offering a purist driving experience that newer, turbocharged, or hybrid Porsches moving forward won't replicate.
*   **Honda S2000 (AP1 / AP2):** Already well on its way. Highly revving (up to 9,000 RPM in early models), lightweight, and famously reliable. Pristine, low-mileage AP2s and Club Racer (CR) editions are commanding high prices.
*   **BMW M2 (F87 Generation, 2016–2021):** Specifically the **M2 Competition** and **M2 CS**. Experts view the F87 as the spiritual successor to the legendary E46 M3—compact, rear-wheel drive, available with a manual, and featuring aggressive widebody styling.
*   **Toyota GR Supra (Manual Transmission, 2023+):** While controversial for sharing parts with BMW, the addition of a 6-speed manual transmission to the 3.0-liter inline-six model instantly turned it into a future classic.

---

### 2. Modern American Muscle (The V8 Swan Song)
With Dodge discontinuing the V8 Challenger/Charger and Chevy ending the Camaro, late-model American V8s are prime targets for collectors.

*   **Ford Shelby GT350 / GT350R (2015–2020):** Fitted with the "Voodoo" 5.2-liter flat-plane crank V8 that revs to 8,250 RPM and was *only* available with a 6-speed manual. Hagerty has flagged this as a guaranteed future blue-chip collectible.
*   **Chevrolet Corvette Z06 (C7 Generation, 2015–2019):** The C7 Z06 is the last front-engine, manual-transmission Corvette ever made. With 650 horsepower from a supercharged V8, low-mileage manual examples are already appreciating.
*   **Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat / Demon:** The ultimate symbols of the 2010s horsepower wars. Hagerty notes that limited-run variants like the **Demon**, **Hellcat Redeye**, and "Last Call" editions will hold immense historical value as the peak of unbridled ICE muscle.

---

### 3. Accessible & Hot Hatch Classics
You don't need six figures to buy a future collectible. Valuation experts frequently point to lightweight, high-fun modern hatchbacks and compacts.

*   **Toyota GR Corolla / GR Yaris:** Built as true rally homologation specials with advanced all-wheel-drive systems and manual transmissions. Low production numbers and glowing critical acclaim guarantee these will be sought after in 15–20 years.
*   **Ford Focus RS (2016–2018):** Featuring a trick AWD system with a famous "Drift Mode," a manual gearbox, and short production runs, the Focus RS stands out as the pinnacle of Ford’s hot-hatch era in North America.
*   **Honda Civic Type R (FK8 & FL5 Generations):** The FK8 introduced the Type R to North America, but the newer FL5 refined it into a near-perfect front-wheel-drive performance car. Both are expected to follow the value trajectory of 1990s Integra Type Rs.
*   **Mazda MX-5 Miata (ND2 Generation, 2019+):** The ND2 update bumped the high-revving engine to 181 hp. Hagerty considers it one of the purest driving experiences ever sold at an affordable price point.

---

### 4. Modern Supercars & Halo Cars

*   **Audi R8 (1st Gen V10 with a "Gated" Manual):** The 2008–2015 R8 combines exotic mid-engine styling, a Lamborghini-derived naturally aspirated V10, and a metallic gated manual shifter. Hagerty included this on their *Bull Market List* as a top pick for growth.
*   **Ferrari 458 Italia (2010–2015):** Highly prized because it is the **last naturally aspirated V8 Ferrari** ever produced. Subsequent models (488, F8, 296 GTB) introduced turbochargers and hybrid systems.
*   **Lexus LFA (2011–2012):** Originally hard to sell at its $375,000 base price, the carbon-fiber LFA with its Yamaha-tuned V10 engine is now widely considered one of the greatest-sounding cars ever made. Values have already surged past $800,000–$1,000,000 and continue to climb.

---

### 5. Cult Trucks and SUVs
The collector market for off-roaders and utility vehicles has exploded in recent years.

*   **Toyota FJ Cruiser (2007–2014):** Retro styling, legendary Toyota reliability, and a manual option on 4WD models. Clean, rust-free FJ Cruisers are already selling for near (and sometimes above) their original MSRP.
*   **Ford F-150 SVT Raptor (1st Gen, 2010–2014):** The truck that started the high-speed desert-running craze. The 1st generation features a naturally aspirated 6.2-liter V8, making it distinct from the twin-turbo V6s that followed.
*   **Jeep Wrangler Rubicon 392 (2021+):** The first factory V8 Wrangler in decades. As emissions regulations tighten, a factory 470-hp V8 Wrangler will be viewed as a glorious anomaly of the early 2020s.

---

### Summary: What Makes a Modern Car Collectible?
According to Hagerty experts, if you are looking to buy a modern car as a potential investment, look for cars that check these boxes:
1. **Manual Transmission:** Automatic versions of the same car rarely appreciate at the same rate.
2. **Naturally Aspirated Engines:** High-revving, non-turbo engines are becoming obsolete.
3. **Low Production / Special Trim:** Base models rarely become valuable; look for "CS," "RS," "TRD," "Z06," or "Type R" badges.
4. **Authenticity:** Unmodified, low-mileage examples with clean history reports always fetch the highest premiums.

**AOL AUTOS** | *Research, Reviews & Buying Advice*

# Future Classics: 10 Cars You Can Buy Right Now That Will Be Collectible in 20 Years

**By AOL Autos Staff**  
*Published in partnership with Hagerty*

Ever wish you had a time machine so you could go back to 1993 and buy a pristine Toyota Supra, or rewind to 1988 to grab a BMW M3 off the dealer lot? We’ve all played the "if only" game with classic cars. But what if you could spot the next million-dollar collectible while it’s still sitting on a showroom floor today?

That’s where the valuation experts at Hagerty come in. 

Every year, the classic car insurance power player releases its highly anticipated **"Hot List"**—a carefully curated lineup of brand-new vehicles (with an MSRP under $100,000) that possess the secret sauce required to become the prized collector cars of tomorrow.

"The key to a future classic isn't just pure speed or a massive price tag—it’s emotional connection," says McKeel Hagerty, CEO of Hagerty. "We look for cars that make your heart race today, because those are the exact vehicles people will be searching for, longing for, and willing to pay top dollar for in 15 to 20 years."

If you’re looking for a fun daily driver that won't turn into a worthless pile of metal in two decades, park your eyes right here. Here are Hagerty’s top 10 contemporary cars destined for future classic stardom.

---

### 1. Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing
* **MSRP:** ~$93,000
* **Why It’s Hot:** 668 horsepower. Supercharged 6.2-liter V8. *Available six-speed manual transmission.* 

In a world rapidly shifting toward quiet, sterile electric vehicles, the CT5-V Blackwing is a glorious, roaring middle finger to conformity. It’s quite possibly the peak of American performance sedans. 

"We are living through the grand finale of the internal combustion era," notes McKeel Hagerty. "High-horsepower, manual-transmission super-sedans like the Blackwing are an endangered species. That rarity and visceral driving experience make it an instant heirloom."

---

### 2. Toyota GR Corolla
* **MSRP:** ~$36,000
* **Why It’s Hot:** Rally-bred, 300-hp turbocharged 3-cylinder, manual only, adjustable AWD system.

Remember the legendary hot hatches of the 1990s? The GR Corolla is their modern, angry grandchild. Developed by Toyota’s Gazoo Racing division, this pocket rocket delivers old-school mechanical grip and raw driver engagement. Lower production numbers mean clean, unmolested examples will command serious cash at auctions in 2040.

---

### 3. Chevrolet Corvette Z06 (C8)
* **MSRP:** ~$110,000 (Base models sneak just under Hagerty's cap)
* **Why It’s Hot:** 670-hp flat-plane crank V8 that revs to 8,600 RPM. 

The mid-engine C8 Stingray was already a game-changer, but the Z06 elevated the Corvette into true supercar territory. Its naturally aspirated LT6 engine is the most powerful atmospheric V8 ever put in a production road car, sounding more like a Ferrari than something built in Kentucky. It is an instant icon.

---

### 4. Honda Civic Type R (FL5)
* **MSRP:** ~$44,700
* **Why It’s Hot:** Peak front-wheel-drive engineering, legendary reliability, razor-sharp handling.

The previous generation Type R was styled like a Transformer, but the current FL5 generation matures the look while refining the drive. Honda manual gearboxes are legendary, and as one of the finest-handling front-wheel-drive cars ever built, the Type R is guaranteed to retain a massive cult following.

---

### 5. Ford Mustang Dark Horse
* **MSRP:** ~$60,000
* **Why It’s Hot:** 500-hp naturally aspirated 5.0L V8, track-focused suspension, menacing styling.

While dodge retired the Challenger and Chevy shelved the Camaro, Ford kept the pony car flame burning. The Dark Horse is the ultimate manifestation of the S650 Mustang platform. 

"When competitors leave a segment, the last car standing becomes a magnet for collectors," says McKeel Hagerty. "The V8 Mustang isn't just a muscle car anymore; it's a piece of American cultural history."

---

### 6. Lexus LC 500
* **MSRP:** ~$99,000
* **Why It’s Hot:** Concept-car styling, bulletproof reliability, naturally aspirated 5.0-liter V8 roar.

Drop-dead gorgeous from every angle, the LC 500 looks like it rolled straight off a motor show turntable and onto the street. While German rivals rely heavily on turbochargers, Lexus stuffed a glorious, high-revving V8 under the hood. It’s a classic Grand Tourer in the truest sense of the word.

---

### 7. Porsche 718 Cayman GTS 4.0
* **MSRP:** ~$97,000
* **Why It’s Hot:** Mid-engine balance, naturally aspirated 4.0-liter flat-six, available manual transmission.

With Porsche announcing that the next-generation 718 line will go fully electric, the clock is ticking on gas-powered Caymans. The GTS 4.0 offers 95% of the hardcore GT4’s performance with everyday usability. Mark our words: collectors will look back on this as one of the sweet spots in Porsche’s legendary history.

---

### 8. BMW M2
* **MSRP:** ~$63,200
* **Why It’s Hot:** Compact footprint, twin-turbo inline-six, rear-wheel drive, manual gearbox.

The modern M3 and M4 have grown into massive, technology-heavy luxury cars. The M2, however, preserves the spirit of the famous E46 M3 from the early 2000s. It’s punchy, aggressive, and a throwback to when BMW's motto "The Ultimate Driving Machine" was felt primarily through the seat of your pants.

---

### 9. Jeep Wrangler Rubicon 392
* **MSRP:** ~$92,000
* **Why It’s Hot:** A 470-hp V8 stuffed inside a factory Wrangler. 

Is it practical? Absolutely not. Is it hilarious fun? Unquestionably. Jeep doing a factory production run of a V8-powered Wrangler was a fever dream that actually came true. Its sheer absurdity and short production lifespan ensure it will be a high-value oddity at future Barrett-Jackson auctions.

---

### 10. Mazda MX-5 Miata RF
* **MSRP:** ~$37,000
* **Why It’s Hot:** Timeless lightweight sports car formula, targa-style power hardtop.

"Miata is always the answer" isn't just a meme—it’s a rule of automotive collecting. The Retractable Fastback (RF) adds striking coupe lines to the pure, lightweight driver's car formula that Mazda mastered back in 1989. Low running costs mean many will be driven into the ground, making clean, well-maintained models hot commodities in 2040.

---

### The Bottom Line

Buying a new car as an "investment" is usually a bad financial plan—depreciation hits fast and hard. But if you choose wisely, you can minimize that drop and eventually ride the curve back up.

"The ultimate advice we give enthusiasts is simple," McKeel Hagerty concludes. "Don’t buy a car just to lock it in a bubble and wait for it to appreciate. Buy the car you love, drive it, take care of it, and enjoy the ride. The fact that it might pay you back in 20 years is just a bonus."

***

**What do you think?** *Which of these future classics would you park in your dream garage today? Let us know in the comments below!*
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Top 10 modern daily drivers that will be worth a fortune in the future AOL Autos list
counterfactuals.output:
AOL Autos published several influential features highlighting **"Future Classics"**—everyday vehicles that possessed the engineering, rarity, or iconic status required to become highly valuable collector cars over time. 

These 10 modern daily drivers capture the essence of AOL Autos' top picks: practical enough to haul groceries or commute in, but built with unique traits (manual transmissions, naturally aspirated V8s, limited production runs) that make them prime candidates to be worth a fortune in the future.

---

### 1. Cadillac CTS-V Wagon (2011–2014)
* **Why it was a daily driver:** It’s a spacious, four-door station wagon with a large trunk and luxury interior.
* **Why it will be worth a fortune:** It features a **556-horsepower supercharged 6.2L LSA V8** straight out of a Chevrolet Corvette, and it was offered with a **6-speed manual transmission**. Cadillac only built around 1,200 manual CTS-V wagons total, making it one of the rarest, most absurdly powerful American cars ever produced. 

### 2. BMW M3 Sedan / Coupe (E90/E92, 2008–2013)
* **Why it was a daily driver:** A refined German sports luxury car available with four doors, modern climate control, and usable back seats.
* **Why it will be worth a fortune:** This was the **only generation of the M3 to ever feature a naturally aspirated V8** (the legendary high-revving 4.0L S65 engine that screamed up to 8,400 RPM). As BMW shifts toward turbocharging and electrification, clean, low-mileage manual E90/E92 M3s are skyrocketing in value.

### 3. Porsche 911 Carrera (997 Generation, 2005–2012)
* **Why it was a daily driver:** Known universally as the "everyday supercar," the 997 offers rear seats for kids or cargo, AWD options (Carrera 4), and excellent reliability.
* **Why it will be worth a fortune:** The 997 is widely considered the "sweet spot" of modern 911s. It was the **last 911 generation to feature hydraulic steering** (giving unmatched road feel) and classic analog proportions before the larger, electric-steering 991 generation took over.

### 4. Chevrolet SS (2014–2017)
* **Why it was a daily driver:** A full-size, unassuming four-door sedan built on an Australian Holden chassis with plenty of legroom and trunk space.
* **Why it will be worth a fortune:** Underneath its subtle exterior sits a **415-hp LS3 V8** paired with magnetic ride control and an optional **6-speed manual gearbox**. Because Chevrolet barely advertised it, production numbers remained extremely low. It is the ultimate "sleeper" muscle car.

### 5. Lexus IS F (2008–2014)
* **Why it was a daily driver:** Bulletproof Toyota reliability, compact luxury sedan comfort, and usability in all weather conditions.
* **Why it will be worth a fortune:** The IS F was Lexus’s first serious attempt to challenge BMW’s M division. It packed a **5.0L naturally aspirated V8** tuned by Yamaha into a compact shell. Given Lexus’s reputation for durability compared to its German rivals, clean examples are becoming prized survivor cars.

### 6. Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 (2015–2020)
* **Why it was a daily driver:** Offers modern Ford infotainment, back seats, a decent trunk, and comfortable magneride suspension modes.
* **Why it will be worth a fortune:** Its heart is the **5.2L "Voodoo" V8**, which features a **flat-plane crankshaft** that revs up to a hair-raising 8,250 RPM. It sounds more like a Ferrari than an American muscle car and was offered exclusively with a 6-speed manual transmission.

### 7. Subaru WRX STI (Final Generation / EJ25 Era, 2015–2021)
* **Why it was a daily driver:** Symmetrical All-Wheel Drive, four doors, high utility, and all-weather capability make it an unmatched year-round commuter.
* **Why it will be worth a fortune:** With Subaru officially retiring the STI badge and discontinuing the ICE-powered rally icon, the final-generation STIs—powered by the iconic, rumbling 2.5L turbocharged EJ engine—have instantly become collector items.

### 8. Chevrolet Corvette C6 Z06 (2006–2013)
* **Why it was a daily driver:** Surprising fuel efficiency on the highway, massive rear hatchback cargo area, and comfortable highway cruising.
* **Why it will be worth a fortune:** The C6 Z06 is powered by the **LS7 7.0-liter (427 cubic inch) naturally aspirated V8**—the largest small-block engine Chevy ever put in a passenger car. Combined with an aluminum frame and a manual-only transmission, it represents peak raw, lightweight American performance.

### 9. Honda Civic Type R (FK8, 2017–2021)
* **Why it was a daily driver:** It’s a Honda Civic hatchback—meaning exceptional practical cargo space, great fuel economy when cruising, and room for five.
* **Why it will be worth a fortune:** The FK8 was the first Civic Type R officially sold in North America. It set front-wheel-drive lap records at the Nürburgring and features one of the absolute best 6-speed manual gearboxes ever engineered. 

### 10. Volkswagen Golf R32 / Golf R (MK5 2008 / MK7 2015–2019)
* **Why it was a daily driver:** The gold standard of practical hot-hatchbacks, featuring luxurious interiors, hatchback utility, and AWD.
* **Why it will be worth a fortune:** 
  * The **MK5 R32** is coveted for its rare **3.2L VR6 engine**, producing an unmistakable exhaust note.
  * The **MK7 Golf R (Manual)** represents the absolute peak of analog Volkswagen performance before digital touchscreens and electrification swept the brand.

---

### What Made These Cars AOL Autos Favorites?
Across AOL Autos' collector analyses, the cars that gained the most value shared four major traits:
1. **The "Last of an Era" Factor:** Naturally aspirated V8s or high-revving engines built right before strict emissions/turbocharging rules took over.
2. **Manual Gearboxes:** Three-pedal setups are rapidly disappearing, making manual variants worth 20% to 50% more on the collector market.
3. **Utility + Performance:** Cars that buyers actually drove (meaning clean, low-mileage examples become exceptionally rare).
4. **Cult Followings:** Vehicles with strong motorsport pedigree or dedicated enthusiast communities.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Provide a detailed top 10 list of cars from the late 2000s that are expected to appreciate in value as collector cars, including models like the Lotus Exige S, Audi S5, and Mustang Shelby GT500 KR.
counterfactuals.output:
The late 2000s (roughly 2005–2010) represents a true "sweet spot" in automotive history. It was an era when manufacturing precision was high enough to produce reliable, high-performing cars, but before modern emissions regulations, electrification, power-assisted electric steering, and ubiquitous automatic transmissions took over. 

As the car industry moves toward electric vehicles and heavily sanitized driving experiences, car enthusiasts are bidding up the price of late-2000s "analog" driver’s cars. 

Here is a detailed breakdown of 10 cars from the late 2000s that are poised for strong value appreciation as future collector icons.

---

### 1. Lotus Exige S (2006–2011)
* **Engine:** Supercharged 1.8L 2ZZ-GE Inline-4 (220 to 257 hp)
* **Transmission:** 6-speed manual
* **Why it will appreciate:** Pure, unadulterated driving purity. The Exige S took the already minimalist Elise formula and turned it into an aggressive, track-focused weapon with a fixed roof, functional aerodynamics, and a supercharger. Weighing around 2,000 lbs, it offers telepathic steering feel that no modern car can replicate. Lotus has now transitioned to heavy electric vehicles (like the Eletre and Evija), making lightweight ICE sports cars like the Exige S historic artifacts of a bygone era.
* **Collector’s Choice:** Look for the late-model **Exige S 260** or **RGB Edition** with low mileage and no fiberglass damage.

### 2. Ford Mustang Shelby GT500KR "King of the Road" (2008–2009)
* **Engine:** Supercharged 5.4L DOHC V8 (540 hp)
* **Transmission:** 6-speed manual
* **Why it will appreciate:** Built to celebrate the 40th anniversary of the original 1968 GT500KR, Ford and Shelby American produced only 1,000 units for North America (matching the original run). It featured a carbon-fiber hood with functional scoops, upgraded SVT suspension, Ford Racing performance parts, and iconic styling. Because of its limited production run and Shelby heritage, it sits in a different tier of collectability compared to standard GT500s.
* **Collector’s Choice:** Factory-original examples in Silver with Blue stripes or Ebony Black with Silver stripes with complete Shelby documentation.

### 3. Audi S5 4.2 Coupe Manual (2008–2012)
* **Engine:** 4.2L Naturally Aspirated FSI V8 (354 hp)
* **Transmission:** 6-speed manual
* **Why it will appreciate:** Designed by Walter de Silva (who called it the most beautiful car he ever designed), the original B8 S5 Coupe has timeless proportions. While the RS5 got a higher-revving V8, the initial S5 offered something rare: a glorious, naturally aspirated 4.2L V8 paired with a 6-speed manual transmission in a sleek, daily-drivable luxury coupe. As clean, unmodified 6-speed V8s become scarce, pristine early S5s are being recognized as bargains with massive upside potential.
* **Collector’s Choice:** Pre-facelift (2008–2011) 6-speed manual coupe with low miles, full maintenance records, and without aftermarket engine tunes.

### 4. BMW M3 (E90 / E92 Generation, 2008–2013)
* **Engine:** 4.0L Naturally Aspirated "S65" V8 (414 hp)
* **Transmission:** 6-speed manual or 7-speed DCT
* **Why it will appreciate:** The E9X generation represents the first and *only* time BMW installed a V8 into a production M3. The S65 V8 revs to a screaming 8,400 RPM and produces an exhaust note that modern turbo engines cannot match. As BMW M-cars become increasingly heavy and digitised, the hydraulic steering and naturally aspirated engine of the E9X generation make it an absolute darling among purists.
* **Collector’s Choice:** E92 Coupes with the Competition Package (ZCP), 6-speed manual, slicktop (no sunroof), in rare colors like Interlagos Blue or Lime Rock Park Edition.

### 5. Audi R8 V10 6-Speed Gated Manual (2009–2012)
* **Engine:** 5.2L Naturally Aspirated V10 (525 hp)
* **Transmission:** 6-speed gated manual
* **Why it will appreciate:** The first-generation R8 was a game-changer, but combining a Lamborghini-derived 5.2-liter V10 with a click-clack **metal gated 6-speed manual gearbox** makes this car an immortal classic. Mid-engine, naturally aspirated V10 cars with manual transmissions will never be built again. Values for gated V10 models have already surpassed their original MSRP and continue to climb.
* **Collector’s Choice:** Coupe models featuring the 6-speed gated manual and the iconic carbon-fiber sideblades.

### 6. Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 "Blue Devil" (2009–2013)
* **Engine:** Supercharged 6.2L "LS9" V8 (638 hp)
* **Transmission:** 6-speed manual
* **Why it will appreciate:** The C6 ZR1 was Chevrolet’s "halo car" statement. Armed with a supercharged LS9 engine, carbon-ceramic brakes, carbon-fiber body panels, and a clear polycarbonate window in the hood, it was an American supercar capable of hitting 205 mph and beating contemporary Ferraris around the Nürburgring. Because it was manual-only and produced in low numbers compared to standard Corvettes, it is destined for blue-chip status.
* **Collector’s Choice:** 2009 model years in Velocity Yellow or Jetstream Blue, or 2012–2013 PDE Performance Package models.

### 7. Porsche 911 GT3 / GT3 RS (997.1 Generation, 2007–2008)
* **Engine:** 3.6L Naturally Aspirated "Mezger" Flat-6 (415 hp)
* **Transmission:** 6-speed manual
* **Why it will appreciate:** The 997.1 GT3 holds a special place in Porsche lore: it was the last standard GT3 generation to feature the legendary, race-derived "Mezger" engine paired exclusively with a manual transmission and hydraulic steering. It strikes the perfect balance between modern usability and visceral, mechanical feedback. Values are already high, but long-term growth is guaranteed.
* **Collector’s Choice:** Low-mileage GT3 RS models in iconic colors (Orange or Signal Green) with carbon bucket seats.

### 8. Mercedes-Benz CLK 63 AMG Black Series (2008)
* **Engine:** 6.2L Naturally Aspirated "M156" V8 (500 hp)
* **Transmission:** 7-speed AMG SPEEDSHIFT
* **Why it will appreciate:** Inspired by the F1 Safety Car, the CLK 63 Black Series was a wild, widebody, rear-wheel-drive hot rod with no rear seats and a raw, booming 6.2L naturally aspirated V8. Only 500 units were brought to the U.S. It represents the absolute pinnacle of AMG’s "muscle car" era, before turbocharging restricted the soundtrack and all-wheel-drive toned down the tail-happy dynamics.
* **Collector’s Choice:** Unmodified, low-mileage examples in Iridium Silver or Obsidian Black with clean car histories.

### 9. Honda S2000 CR - Club Racer (2008–2009)
* **Engine:** 2.2L Naturally Aspirated F22C1 Inline-4 (237 hp)
* **Transmission:** 6-speed manual
* **Why it will appreciate:** The standard S2000 is already a rising classic, but the "Club Racer" (CR) edition is the holy grail. Honda removed the soft top, air conditioning, and radio (to save weight), then added a body kit, stiffer suspension, a tonneau cover, a hardtop, and a faster steering rack. Only 699 units were sold in the U.S., making it one of the rarest mainstream Japanese sports cars of the modern era.
* **Collector’s Choice:** Apex Blue Pearl models with the delete options (no A/C or audio system from factory).

### 10. Dodge Viper SRT-10 ACR (2008–2010)
* **Engine:** 8.4L Naturally Aspirated V10 (600 hp)
* **Transmission:** 6-speed manual
* **Why it will appreciate:** The Viper ACR (American Club Racer) was an uncompromising street-legal race car. Armed with an 8.4-liter V10 engine, a massive carbon fiber wing, two-way adjustable KW coilovers, and aggressive front splitters, it set track records across the globe (including an 7:12 lap at the Nürburgring). It represents the absolute extreme of the "huge displacement, manual transmission, no driver aids" formula.
* **Collector’s Choice:** 1-of-50 "Final Edition" models (2010) or cars featuring the iconic two-tone ACR paint schemes with the Hardcore Package.

---

### Summary: What Makes Late 2000s Cars Collectible?

When shopping in this era for investment potential, prioritize cars that feature:
1. **Naturally Aspirated high-RPM engines** or large-displacement V8s/V10s.
2. **Manual Transmissions** (gated manuals commanding the highest premium).
3. **Hydraulic power steering** (offering true road feel over modern electric racks).
4. **Low production/special edition trims** (Black Series, GT3 RS, GT500KR, CR).
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: I want to buy a car today that might be a collector's item in 20 years. Can you list 10 modern cars with high potential for future appreciation, along with brief specs for each?
counterfactuals.output:
Investing in modern cars for future appreciation is largely about identifying **"the last of an era."** As the automotive industry shifts to electrification and automation, cars featuring internal combustion engines (especially naturally aspirated ones), manual transmissions, low production numbers, and analog driving experiences will likely command high premiums in 20 years.

Here are 10 modern cars (currently available or produced within the last 3–4 years) with exceptionally high potential to become sought-after collector items by 2044.

---

### 1. Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 RS (2022–Present)
* **Specs:** 4.0L Naturally Aspirated Flat-6 | 493 hp | 331 lb-ft torque | 7-Speed PDK | 0–60 mph: 3.2s
* **Why it will appreciate:** It is widely considered the ultimate mid-engine Porsche. It houses the engine directly out of the 911 GT3 that revs to 9,000 RPM, with air intakes right behind the driver's ears. As Porsche transitions the 718 line to full EV, the GT4 RS stands as the absolute pinnacle of mid-engine internal combustion.

### 2. Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing (2022–Present)
* **Specs:** 6.2L Supercharged V8 | 668 hp | 659 lb-ft torque | 6-Speed Manual (or 10-Speed Auto) | 0–60 mph: 3.4s
* **Why it will appreciate:** This is the swan song for the American super-sedan. It combines a massive, supercharged V8 with a traditional 6-speed manual transmission in a rear-wheel-drive chassis. It beats European competitors in driving dynamics and represents an era of unhinged American performance that will never return. *(Note: The manual version will hold the highest value).*

### 3. Chevrolet Corvette C8 Z06 (2023–Present)
* **Specs:** 5.5L Flat-Plane Crank NA V8 (LT6) | 670 hp | 460 lb-ft torque | 8-Speed Dual-Clutch | 0–60 mph: 2.6s
* **Why it will appreciate:** The LT6 engine in the Z06 is the highest-horsepower naturally aspirated V8 ever put into a production road car, revving to 8,600 RPM. It sounds like an exotic Ferrari supercar but carries American heritage. Production issues and high demand mean clean, low-mileage examples will be prized.

### 4. Lotus Emira (V6 Manual) (2023–Present)
* **Specs:** 3.5L Supercharged V6 (Toyota-sourced) | 400 hp | 310 lb-ft torque | 6-Speed Manual | 0–60 mph: 4.2s
* **Why it will appreciate:** Lotus has officially declared the Emira to be their **final internal combustion car ever made**. Featuring hydraulic steering, a supercharged V6, a exposed manual shift linkage, and stunning exotic looks, this is guaranteed to be a centerpiece for collectors of pure driver's cars.

### 5. Lexus LC 500 Coupe (2018–Present)
* **Specs:** 5.0L Naturally Aspirated V8 | 471 hp | 398 lb-ft torque | 10-Speed Auto | 0–60 mph: 4.4s
* **Why it will appreciate:** Modern cars rarely become design icons immediately, but the LC 500 did. Beyond its concept-car looks, it features a reliable, high-revving, naturally aspirated V8 engine in an era dominated by turbos and hybrids. Its combination of Japanese reliability, drop-dead gorgeous styling, and V8 soundtrack guarantees classic status.

### 6. Toyota GR Corolla Morizo Edition (2023)
* **Specs:** 1.6L Turbocharged 3-Cylinder | 300 hp | 295 lb-ft torque | 6-Speed Manual | AWD | 0–60 mph: 4.9s
* **Why it will appreciate:** A modern "homologation special" rally car for the road. The Morizo Edition is limited to just 200 units worldwide for its launch year, featuring rear-seat delete, extra structural bracing, shorter gearing, and higher torque. Limited-production Japanese performance cars (like the Subaru 22B) have historically skyrocketed in value.

### 7. Honda Civic Type R - FL5 Generation (2023–Present)
* **Specs:** 2.0L Turbocharged Inline-4 | 315 hp | 310 lb-ft torque | 6-Speed Manual | FWD | 0–60 mph: 4.9s
* **Why it will appreciate:** The FL5 is widely regarded by journalists as the peak of front-wheel-drive chassis engineering. It will almost certainly be the last non-hybrid, purely gasoline-powered Civic Type R with a manual transmission. Clean, unmodified Type R models always appreciate over a 20-year horizon.

### 8. Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 (2020–2022)
* **Specs:** 5.2L Supercharged V8 ("Predator") | 760 hp | 625 lb-ft torque | 7-Speed Dual-Clutch | 0–60 mph: 3.3s
* **Why it will appreciate:** With 760 horsepower, it is the most powerful street-legal factory Ford ever built. Featuring carbon-fiber wheels (Track Pack), a cross-plane supercharged V8, and track capabilities that rival European supercars, top-tier Shelby Mustangs historically always become high-value auction darlings.

### 9. BMW M2 CS - F87 Generation (2020)
* **Specs:** 3.0L Twin-Turbo Inline-6 | 444 hp | 406 lb-ft torque | 6-Speed Manual (or 7-Speed DCT) | 0–60 mph: 3.8s
* **Why it will appreciate:** Produced for only one model year in very limited quantities (around 2,200 globally), the F87 M2 CS is considered by BMW purists to be the best modern M-car built in the last 15 years. Perfect proportions, aggressive styling, carbon fiber everywhere, and available in a manual.

### 10. Alfa Romeo Giulia Quadrifoglio / GTA (2017–2024)
* **Specs (Standard QV):** 2.9L Twin-Turbo V6 (Ferrari-derived) | 505 hp | 443 lb-ft torque | 8-Speed Auto | 0–60 mph: 3.8s
* **Why it will appreciate:** Driven by a Ferrari-developed engine, the Giulia Quadrifoglio restored Alfa Romeo’s reputation for making soul-stirring sport sedans. Because Alfa Romeo is transitioning to EVs, and because Italian cars always carry emotional weight, low-mileage Quadrifoglios (especially ultra-rare GTAm variants) will be hot commodities.

---

### Key Rules for Maximum Appreciation:
If buying one of these today as a future investment, keep these four factors in mind:
1. **Choose the Manual:** When available (e.g., CT5-V, Emira, M2, GT4 RS/GT3, CTR), manual transmissions will command a 30% to 50% premium over automatics in 20 years.
2. **Buy Special/Rare Trims:** Base models rarely appreciate. Focus on limited editions, track packages, or launch editions (e.g., Morizo, GT4 RS, CS).
3. **Color Matters:** Unique, historic, or high-impact colors (e.g., Porsche Paint to Sample, BMW Individual colors, bright Shelby blues/stripes) hold significantly more value than silver, white, or black.
4. **Preserve Condition:** Keep miles low, preserve all original paperwork/stickers, and keep the car in 100% stock condition (avoid aftermarket modifications).
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
